1.w: [“] And now they laugh at me, the fewer in days than I, whose fathers I disdained to put with the dogs of my flock.

2.w: Indeed, the strength of their hands, what [is it] to me? Upon them vigor has perished,

3.w: in poverty and in harsh hunger, ones gnawing the dry ground by night, [in] ruin and desolation.

4.w: They [are] plucking mallow among the brush, and the root of the broom tree is their bread.

5.w: From the midst of people they are driven out; they shout at them as [at] a thief.

6.w: On the slope of wadis [they are] to dwell, in holes of the dust and rocks.

7.w: Among the shrubs they bray; under the nettles they huddle together.

8.w: Sons of a fool, even sons without a name, they were scourged from the land.

9.w: And now I have become their song, and I have become a byword among them.

10.w: They abhor me [and] keep far from me; and from my face they do not withhold spit.

11.w: For my bowstring he has loosed and afflicted me, and they have cast [off] the bridle before me.

12.w: On the right a brood arises; they push away my feet, and they build up against me the ways of destruction.

13.w: They break up my path; they advance my calamity, with no one helping them.

14.w: As a wide breach they come; amid the ruin they roll on.

15.w: Terrors are turned over upon me; like the wind it pursues my honor, and like a cloud my deliverance has passed away.

16.w: And now within me my soul is poured out; days of affliction seize me.

17.w: Night pierces my bones from upon me, and my gnawing pains will not lie down.

18.w: With abundance of strength He grasps my garment; by the collar of my tunic He seizes me.

19.w: He has cast me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.

20.w: I cry out to You, but You do not answer me; I stand up, and You gaze at me.

21.w: You have turned to [be] cruel toward me; with the strength of Your hand You oppose me.

22.w: You lift me up to the wind and make me ride [it], You toss me about in the storm.

23.w: For I know [that] You will bring me [to] death, and [to] the house of appointment to all the living.

24.w: Surely one does not stretch out a hand against the oppressed, when in his ruin he cries out to [him].

25.w: If not did I weep for the harshness of day, [while] my soul grieved for the needy one?

26.w: And, I hoped for good, and evil came; and I waited for light, and darkness came.

27.w: My bowels have boiled and they do not rest; days of affliction confront me.

28.w: I go about darkened, not by the sun; I rise up in the assembly [and] cry out.

29.w: I have become a brother to jackals, and a companion to the daughters of the ostrich.

30.w: My skin turns black and falls from me, and my bone burns with heat.

31.w: And my harp is changed to mourning, and my flute to the voice of weeping.
